ai.description: This 5–7 cm frog is vibrant emerald green with white-spotted flanks. It features large, fully webbed feet with orange discs and prominent, horizontally elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Zhangixalus smaragdinus* is best distinguished by its vibrant, uniform emerald-green dorsum that lacks the distinct dark dorsal spots or mottling found in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Nepal Flying Frog inhabits subtropical broadleaf forests and moist temperate woodlands, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nepal Flying Frog is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its large, webbed feet to glide between trees and escape predators when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Zhangixalus smaragdinus* breeds in foam nests suspended over water during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nepal Flying Frog occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, primarily across Nepal and India's West Bengal and Sikkim states, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nepal Flying Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard from vegetation surrounding forest pools during the monsoon season.
